status_note: benchmark not built: free official inputs are partial and mostly proxies. Sourced: grid intensity (CEA CO2 baseline database xlsx, Ember), car stock 1991-2020 (MoRTH Road Transport Year Book Table 2.1, data.gov.in GODL API to 2017), NDC anchor (2022 updated NDC, intensity target only). Missing or proxy-only: passenger-car CO2 (UNFCCC BUR/BTR give whole road transport at 2016, 2020, 2022 only, no car split; BTR1 CRT xlsx must be fetched by hand from unfccc.int/documents/656940), annual km per car (no survey; Goel et al. 2015 Delhi 12,200 km), vehicle age (none published), certified technology by model (BEE CAFE reports OEM averages only; MIDC cycle). S2 would be FLAG (no absolute or sector target). More than half the inputs proxied, so any result would be direction-only under guideline 5.3. Model-level sales are not free: Hyundai Motor India and Kia India publish company totals only, SIAM model data is paid, Vahan's public report hides the model and exports by hand behind a CAPTCHA.

benchmark not built yet: the Japan destination inputs were scouted on 2026-09-04 and are better than Korea's. Passenger-car CO2 is published as a row (GIO/NIES allocated-sector sheet, 1990 to FY2024, and the UNFCCC common reporting table 1.A.3.b.i Cars, the two agreeing to 0.01 %); certified gCO2/km per model and grade comes from MLIT 自動車燃費一覧; stock from AIRIA; distance from the MLIT fuel-consumption survey (7,835 km per car in FY2025). Three inputs are proxied or withheld: the stock age distribution is only in a paid AIRIA book (mean age 9.44 years for registered cars and 9.80 for kei is the free substitute), no free Japanese list gives battery-electric Wh/km or plug-in utility factors, and the 2025 climate plan publishes no transport sector target so S2 must use the superseded 2021 plan (224 to 146 MtCO2e by FY2030). Sales held: JADA nameplate registrations (top 50, kei and foreign brands excluded) and the maker fuel mix; no Japanese publisher crosses model with powertrain.
